target_customer: Independent birth and postpartum doulas, and the California families and insurers (Medi-Cal and commercial plans) that pay for their care
problem: Doulas face a steep learning curve and heavy paperwork to accept insurance, so most families pay out of pocket or go without doula care.
business_model: Software platform and provider network that bills insurers and takes a share of reimbursed visits (exact take not found)
product_category: Healthcare provider network and revenue cycle platform for doulas

founders.name: Lindsey Redd
previous_startups: Onu (co-founded with Chine Ikoro, per YC page; Onu's relationship to Loula is not clear)
founders.background_notes: Software engineer at Lyft and Stripe per the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Credentialing, contracting and claims workflows are standard software integration; the hard part is payer operations rather than technology.

defensibility.rationale: A credentialed provider network with payer contracts takes time to build, though other networks can replicate it.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Pomelo Care acquired The Doula Network (reported 2024-09) to offer a hybrid maternity model; Flourish Care raised a $5.7M seed for doula care in March 2026. No sign these affected Loula directly.

market_need_then: California added a Medi-Cal doula benefit in January 2023 through CalAIM, but sources report slow uptake because paperwork and rates deterred doulas; private plans rarely covered doulas and families typically paid $2,500 to $3,500 out of pocket.

branding.domain_note: Uses joinloula.com, a prefixed domain rather than loula.com.

identity.voice_and_tone: Family-facing, 'we handle the billing and paperwork' framing

branding.community_and_virality: Coverage in People of Color in Tech; no wider community evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Small niche brand with limited press; a warm, doula-sounding name but not explained by any source.

outcome_analysis: Loula is active with seven people on the YC page and claims over 400 California doulas, 2,500 families and 18,000 visits on its own site. A public launch in early 2025 and the Medi-Cal benefit gave it a tailwind, while federal Medicaid cuts are a reported risk to demand. Funding is not verifiable, so its capacity to scale beyond California is unclear.
notes: Funding aggregators conflict: Dealroom $125K seed, Simplify $130K, ZeroG $250K pre-seed (2024-03), CB Insights $500K with Meridian Street Capital and Y Combinator. All unverified aggregator figures, so no round recorded. Flourish Care's $5.7M seed is a different company. Search snippets say public launch was February 2025 with about 30 doulas, while YC lists the batch as W23 and founded 2022. No competitor source dated near the batch was found, so the list is empty. The YC page includes a launch post for Onu, a separate company, not used for Loula facts.
